name: COVIDx CXR-3
description: After more than two years since the beginning of the COVID-19 pandemic, the pressure of this crisis continues to devastate globally. The use of chest X-ray (CXR) imaging as a complementary screening strategy to RT-PCR testing is not only prevailing but has greatly increased due to its routine clinical use for respiratory complaints. Thus far, many visual perception models have been proposed for COVID-19 screening based on CXR imaging. Nevertheless, the accuracy and the generalization capacity of these models are very much dependent on the diversity and the size of the dataset they were trained on. Motivated by this, we introduce COVIDx CXR-3, a large-scale benchmark dataset of CXR images for supporting COVID-19 computer vision research. COVIDx CXR-3 is composed of 30,386 CXR images from a multinational cohort of 17,026 patients from at least 51 countries, making it, to the best of our knowledge, the most extensive, most diverse COVID-19 CXR dataset in open access form. Here, we provide comprehensive details on the various aspects of the proposed dataset including patient demographics, imaging views, and infection types. The hope is that COVIDx CXR-3 can assist scientists in advancing machine learning research against both the COVID-19 pandemic and related diseases.
evaluation_method: AUC (ROC) and accuracy; sensitivity/specificity commonly reported in medical settings
typical_sota_score: AUC ~0.85–0.98 (varies by model, split, and class definitions)
reputation: One of the largest openly available COVID chest X-ray collections and commonly used in academic research, though used with caution due to label/source heterogeneity.
notes: Heterogeneous multi-source dataset with label noise and class imbalance; potential patient/source overlap if splits are not carefully controlled; not a substitute for clinical validation.
